keyVerseText: And Hadad found great favour in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him to wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
rootMeaning: The term תַּחְפְּנֵיס (Tachpᵉnêyç) is of Egyptian derivation, indicating its origin outside the Hebrew linguistic tradition. While no specific Hebrew root is provided, the name functions as a proper noun identifying a female figure of high status, specifically a queen. This etymological background underscores the word's association with royalty and foreign influence within the biblical narrative, highlighting the cultural and political intersections present in the text.
usageInScripture: The word תַּחְפְּנֵיס appears three times in Scripture, consistently translated as "of Tahpenes," referring to an Egyptian queen. Its usage is tightly focused, naming a particular individual who is identified as the wife of the king during the time of David and Solomon. This consistency in translation and limited occurrence emphasizes the term's role as a proper name rather than a common noun, marking a specific historical and relational identity within the biblical account.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding תַּחְפְּנֵיס as the name of an Egyptian queen married into the Israelite royal family reveals the complex interplay between God's chosen people and surrounding nations. This inclusion of a foreign queen in the biblical narrative points to God's sovereignty over all peoples and the unfolding of His providential plan through diverse individuals and cultures. It also illustrates the reality of covenantal faithfulness amidst political alliances and the challenges of maintaining spiritual purity. Recognizing Tahpenes' role invites reflection on how God's purposes are fulfilled even through imperfect human relationships and worldly power structures.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Kings 11:19, the verse notes that Hadad found favor with Pharaoh, who gave him the sister of his wife, identified as the sister of Tahpenes the queen. The mention of Tahpenes here situates this political marriage within the royal household, emphasizing her status and influence. The use of her name highlights the interconnectedness of royal families and the significance of these alliances, reminding readers that God's providence operates within historical realities and personal relationships.
